title: Serving Runtime — Architecture, Kernel Scheduling, Profiling Playbooks, Benchmarking Suite, Runbooks, and Release Notes
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the serving runtime team’s canonical reference: architecture overview, kernel scheduling strategy, profiling and benchmarking playbooks, operational runbooks, known issues, and recent release notes. It is intended for engineers onboarding to the serving runtime, SREs operating inference fleets, and product/PMs who need a technical grounding in how inference is served and measured at Redwood.

Sections
1) Runtime architecture overview
2) Kernel selection and scheduling policy
3) Profiling playbook (how to reproduce and triage perf regressions)
4) Benchmarking suite (tests, metrics, and CI hooks)
5) Runtime runbooks (incident response and common procedures)
6) Known issues and workarounds
7) Recent release notes (summary)

---

1) Runtime architecture overview

Short intro: Redwood's serving runtime is a modular, GPU-optimized inference engine that supports transformer-based models with features to minimize latency and cost: continuous batching, KV cache management, quantization paths, and dynamic kernel selection. Key goals: predictable P99 latency within SLOs, high throughput for bursty workloads, and graceful degradation via routing/fallback policies.

Primary components:
- Frontend API Gateway: authenticates, enforces quotas, and routes to the runtime (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Router / Smart Router: policy engine that selects region, capacity tier, and model variant.
- Worker Process (runtime): hosts the model, performs token generation, manages KV cache, and interacts with GPU kernels.
- Scheduler: per-host job queue + kernel-level scheduler that orders and coalesces inference traces into batches.
- Cache Layer: persistent prefix/KV cache (in-memory + optional redis backing) used to short-circuit repeated prefixes.
- Telemetry & Tracing: OpenTelemetry spans, token-level counters, and per-request cost attribution exported to observability.

SLOs and ownership:
- P95 latency target: 50ms for short-text (<= 128 tokens) on Dedicated tier (single-token generation).
- P99 latency target: 200ms for short-text on Dedicated tier.
- Throughput SLO: sustain 8000 tokens/sec per p4d-8x cluster under 75% GPU utilization (example target; cluster sizing owned by eng-sre).
- Owner: eng-serving-runtime (primary), eng-sre (capacity + infra), eng-platform (observability).

Deployment modes and variant handling:
- Each runtime binary supports FP32/FP16/INT8 execution modes and exposes quantization profiles.
- Model variants are published to the model catalog with capability tags (latency_class, mem_footprint, quant_profile_id). Router will fall back to a compatible variant if primary is degraded.

---

2) Kernel selection and scheduling policy

Principles:
- Minimize head-of-line blocking: prefer many small batches coalesced quickly rather than waiting long for a single large batch.
- Sequence-aware kernel choice: select kernels based on sequence length histograms and attention type (dense vs. flash attention).
- Prioritize latency-SLO traffic: low-latency routes get preemptive scheduling and smaller max-batch sizes.

Kernel selection flow (high-level):
1. On model load, gather model metadata (hidden_size, num_heads, layer_norm_type, supported kernels).
2. Runtime consults runtime-kernel-table (calibrated per hardware) to rank kernels by expected token throughput and memory footprint for observed sequence length percentile.
3. Pick kernel variant with lowest estimated P99 for the current request class while satisfying memory headroom constraints.

Scheduling policies (configurable flags):
- batch.max_wait_ms (default 8ms for latency-tier, 30ms for throughput-tier)
- batch.max_tokens (max tokens per batch: default 4096)
- schedule.preempt_threshold (fractional GPU util threshold to allow preemption: default 0.85)
- schedule.kv_cache_priority (boolean; true to prefer cached prefix fast-paths)

Example scheduling config table:
| config_key | default | description |
| batch.max_wait_ms | "8" | Max time to wait before forcing a batch dispatch (latency tier). |
| batch.max_wait_ms_throughput | "30" | Max wait for throughput-optimized routes. |
| batch.max_tokens | "4096" | Maximum tokens to coalesce in a single dispatch. |
| schedule.preempt_threshold | "0.85" | GPU util fraction above which low-priority work will be throttled or queued. |

Runtime knobs for engineers (CLI examples):
- To view active scheduling config: rruntimectl get-config --env=prod --host=worker-12
- To toggle preemption on a host: rruntimectl set-config --host=worker-12 schedule.preempt_threshold=0.7 --reload

---

3) Profiling playbook (how to reproduce and triage perf regressions)

Goal: provide reproducible steps to capture perf regressions from observed alerts to root cause and remediation.

Quick triage checklist:
1. Confirm alert context: metric, host, time window, route/model, and recent config changes.
2. Collect traces: request trace id, worker logs, GPU metrics (nvidia-smi or telem), and OTel spans.
3. Reproduce locally (if possible) with the same model, weights, sequence length distribution, and workload.

Profiling steps (detailed):
1. Capture a full trace: rruntimectl capture-trace --trace-id=<id> --duration=60s --output=/tmp/trace.json
2. Capture GPU counters: nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 10 -o TD > /tmp/gpu_dmon.txt (or use perfcollect script).
3. Run microbenchmarks: use bench-runner to execute single-layer and full-forward passes at the target sequence length and batch sizes: bench-runner --model <model> --seq 128 --batch 4 --profile=nvtx --out /tmp/bench.json
4. Compare to baseline benchmarks captured in /opt/benchmarks/baseline-<model>-<hw>.json.

Interpreting results:
- High idle GPU but high latency: likely scheduling or kernel mismatch (small batches being dispatched inefficiently).
- High SM utilization but memory errors: kernel memory footprint exceeded; check quantization profile and reduce batch.max_tokens.
- Spikes in memcpy time: PCIe/NVLink contention or large KV cache misses; check host-level I/O and cache hit rates.

Common remediation steps:
- Adjust batch.max_wait_ms down for high-latency routes to reduce queueing.
- Force an alternative kernel: rruntimectl set-kernel --host worker-12 --model <model> --kernel flash_attention_v2 --reload
- Patch: if NVTX shows excessive memcpy from redis, increase redis connection pool and enable async prefetch.

---

4) Benchmarking suite (tests, metrics, and CI hooks)

Test categories:
- Microbenchmarks: single-GPU kernel latency and per-layer forward/backward timings.
- Macrobenchmarks: end-to-end RT generation over representative prompt sets (short, medium, long).
- Stability tests: 72-hour soak with randomized prompt mix to validate memory growth and KV cache correctness.

Key metrics collected:
- tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency (per-token and per-request), GPU utilization, memory headroom, batch sizes, cache hit ratio, and per-request cost estimate.

CI integration:
- PRs to runtime must include benchmark check: ./ci/run_benchmarks.sh --model <model> --hw=p4d --baseline=baseline.json
- Bench results are uploaded to BenchDB and a regression alert is triggered if p99 latency increases by >10% or tokens/sec drops by >8%.

Bench naming convention and storage:
- File name: bench-<model>-<hw>-YYYYMMDD.json
- Storage: s3://redwood-bench/serving-runtime/<model>/

Example command to run the macro benchmark locally:
- ./bench-runner --scenario macro-short --model redwood-llama-13b --hw local-p4d --concurrency 50 --out bench-output.json

5) Runtime runbooks (incident response and common procedures)

Runbook: High P99 latency on Dedicated cluster
1. Verify alert details in PagerDuty and look up affected host via alert tags.
2. Run rruntimectl inspect --host <host> --last 15m and review batch queue lengths and batch.max_wait_ms.
3. If batch queue is long and GPU utilization low, restart scheduler process: systemctl restart rruntime-scheduler && monitor for 5 minutes.
4. If GPU utilization saturated, check for noisy neighbor model; use router to migrate lower-priority traffic: rrouterctl migrate-route --route <route> --to-node-group best-effort
5. Escalate to eng-sre if cluster-level capacity is exhausted.

Runbook: Model failed to load on host during deploy
1. Inspect logs: journalctl -u rruntime-worker -n 200.
2. Check disk space under /mnt/models and file permissions (uid/gid).
3. If OOM during load, reduce concurrency or pin a lighter quantized variant and re-deploy.

Standard runbook hygiene:
- Post-incident: prepare a 1-page summary with timeline, root cause, and remediation.
- Ownership: incidents impacting customer SLAs should have an assigned lead and remediation PR linked within 48 hours.

---

6) Known issues and workarounds (tracked issues with status)

- Issue: intermittent P99 spikes on p4d with long-context (>2048) sequences when using flash_attention_v2.
  - Symptoms: periodic 2-3x P99 increases, SM utilization drops during spike.
  - Workaround: force kernel flash_attention_fallback or use batch.max_wait_ms=5 for affected route.
  - Planned fix: kernel vendor patch scheduled in 2028-07 release.

- Issue: KV cache misses under heavy concurrent prefix writes to redis causing memcpy hotspots.
  - Workaround: enable local in-memory cache for high-throughput tenants and increase redis maxclients.

- Issue: occasional model load failures after upgrade when quant_profile mismatch present.
  - Workaround: run model-validator before deploy: model-validator --model <pkg> --verify-quant-profile

Reference list: detailed ticket list is maintained in Jira board RUNTIME-ISSUES. Always cross-link to ticket IDs in postmortems.

---

7) Recent release notes (summary)

Release 2028-05-28 (v4.12.0) — Major
- New: dynamic kernel ranking service (pilot) that autocalibrates kernel selection per host.
- Perf: reduced p99 for short-text by ~18% on p4d-8x in throughput tier.
- Ops: added rruntimectl set-kernel command and safe-reload support.
- Fix: mitigated a KV cache race that caused cache corruption under heavy writes.

Release 2028-03-10 (v4.11.3) — Patch
- Fix: corrected memory leak when switching quantization profiles on the fly.
- Fix: improved telemetry to include batch size histograms.

Upgrade notes and rolling strategy:
- Default upgrade window: 02:00-06:00 UTC for non-global customers.
- Strategy: canary 3 hosts -> 10% of fleet -> 50% -> 100%.
- If p99 increases > 12% during canary, auto-rollback to previous revision.
